Class WhoApiKeyAutoConfiguration

java.lang.Object
org.jwcarman.who.autoconfigure.WhoApiKeyAutoConfiguration
@AutoConfiguration(after=WhoAutoConfiguration.class) @EnableConfigurationProperties(WhoProperties.class) @ConditionalOnClass(name="org.jwcarman.who.apikey.ApiKeyAuthenticationFilter") @ConditionalOnBooleanProperty(name="who.api-key.enabled", matchIfMissing=true) public class WhoApiKeyAutoConfiguration extends Object
Registers API key beans when who-apikey is on the classpath.

    • apiKeyService

      @Bean @ConditionalOnMissingBean public ApiKeyService apiKeyService(ApiKeyCredentialRepository apiKeyCredentialRepository, CredentialIdentityRepository credentialIdentityRepository, PermissionsResolver permissionsResolver, ApiKeyFormat apiKeyFormat, WhoProperties properties, WhoEventPublisher whoEventPublisher, Clock clock)
      Makes, lists, rotates and revokes API keys, publishing the credential events.
      Parameters:
      apiKeyCredentialRepository - stores the keys
      credentialIdentityRepository - links keys to identities
      permissionsResolver - what an owner holds, checked against a new key's scopes
      apiKeyFormat - makes the keys
      properties - who.api-key.max-lifetime
      whoEventPublisher - where the credential events are published
      clock - stamps keys and events
      Returns:
      the service
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if the maximum lifetime is not positive, so startup fails

    • apiKeyAuthenticationFilter

      @Bean @ConditionalOnMissingBean public ApiKeyAuthenticationFilter apiKeyAuthenticationFilter(ApiKeyCredentialRepository apiKeyCredentialRepository, WhoService whoService, ApiKeyFormat apiKeyFormat, WhoProperties properties, WhoEventPublisher whoEventPublisher, Clock clock)
      The API key filter. Its provider is not a bean, so it never joins the application's global authentication manager.
      Parameters:
      apiKeyCredentialRepository - looks keys up by their hash and records their use
      whoService - resolves a key's credential to its identity
      apiKeyFormat - checks a key's shape before any lookup
      properties - the header name and who.api-key.last-used-interval
      whoEventPublisher - where API key sign-ins are published
      clock - decides expiry and stamps the events
      Returns:
      the filter
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if the last-used interval is not positive, so startup fails

      Mounts the filter in a chain built with WhoSecurity.all(), and exempts requests that carry a key from CSRF.

      Returns:

    • apiKeyEndpoints

      @Bean @ConditionalOnMissingBean public ApiKeyEndpoints apiKeyEndpoints(ApiKeyService apiKeyService, WhoSessionSecurityContextRepository sessionRepository, org.springframework.beans.factory.ObjectProvider<WhoExceptionHandoff> handoff, org.springframework.beans.factory.ObjectProvider<tools.jackson.databind.json.JsonMapper> jsonMapper, Clock clock, WhoProperties properties, WhoPaths paths)
      The caller's API keys at /me/api-keys under who.base-path, on every browser chain and every stateless chain.

      sessionRepository - reads the browser's who session and its sign-in time

      clock - the current time
      properties - who.security.recent-sign-in
      paths - where the endpoints live
      Returns:
      the endpoints
